questions.title: What should you do if two golf balls are really close together?
questions.question: If your ball and your friend’s ball are almost touching on the grass, and you need to hit your ball but the other ball is in your way, what should you do?

choices.text: Pick up and wipe both balls, then hit your shots.
Put a marker next to your friend’s ball and pick it up (don’t clean it), hit your shot, then put your friend’s ball back where it was.
Try to hit your ball without moving either ball, even if it’s hard.
Both balls must be dropped somewhere else on the grass.

questions.explanation: You should put a marker where your friend’s ball is and pick it up without cleaning it. After you take your shot, put your friend’s ball back in the same place.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A small coin or plastic piece you put on the ground to remember where the ball was.
Put the ball back in exactly the same spot it was before.

questions.teachingTip: Act out the situation with two balls. Let the children practise marking, lifting, and putting the ball back.
likelyMisconceptions: Children may think both balls need to be moved away or cleaned every time.
They may try to play around the ball instead of marking and lifting it.

questions.title: What to do when two balls are very close together
questions.question: Two golf balls are so close together on the fairway that one player's stroke would be affected. What should happen next?

choices.text: Pick up and clean both balls, then play.
Mark and lift the other player's ball (without cleaning it), play your own shot, then replace their ball.
Try to play without moving either ball, even if it's difficult.
Both balls must be dropped in a different spot.

questions.explanation: When two balls interfere with each other, one player's ball can be marked and lifted (without cleaning). After the other player's shot, the ball is replaced in its original spot.
